title: IRGC Fires Anti-Ship Ballistic Missiles at US Carrier and Destroyer in Strait of Hormuz — Both Evade
detail: Early Sept 5 (Day 191), the IRGC Navy fired anti-ship ballistic missiles — reportedly launched from Isfahan and Kerman provinces — at a US Navy aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer patrolling the Strait of Hormuz. Both vessels evaded the incoming fire; CENTCOM has not disclosed whether maneuver, decoys, electronic warfare, or interceptors were used. No US personnel were injured and neither ship was hit, though Iran claims the vessels were damaged — an assertion CENTCOM has not corroborated. CENTCOM chief Adm. Brad Cooper warned: 'If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost.' Hours later the US struck three Iranian oil tankers in retaliation.

media.caption: US Navy vessels in the Gulf region amid renewed Iran-US strikes, Sept 5, 2026

confidenceReason: CENTCOM confirmed the missile launch and that both ships evaded; Iran's claim of damage to the vessels is uncorroborated and disputed by the US.

title: US Strikes 3 Iranian Oil Tankers Near Kharg Island, Jask, and Gulf of Oman in Retaliation
detail: Hours after the IRGC's failed ballistic-missile attack on a US carrier and destroyer, CENTCOM struck three Iranian crude oil tankers it says were financing IRGC regional proxies: M/T Downy near Kharg Island (Iran's main oil export hub) was permanently disabled, M/T Stark 1 near Jask was permanently disabled, and M/T Kylo (also referenced as Noxen) was struck and destroyed in the Gulf of Oman — the vessel's crew evacuated before it sank. No casualties were reported. CENTCOM said the three tankers had been supporting IRGC-linked proxy financing. Iran's Foreign Ministry condemned the strikes as an escalation and vowed retaliation.

title: Trump Threatens US Could Strike Iran's 'Pickaxe Mountain' Nuclear Site 'Very Soon'
detail: Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office, President Trump said the US could strike Pickaxe Mountain — a deeply buried underground complex roughly 2km from the Natanz enrichment plant in Isfahan province — 'very soon,' claiming Washington knows 'everybody that's moving' at the site. Dug more than 300 feet under solid granite, the facility is significantly deeper than Fordow and was untouched in prior US/Israeli strikes because it was believed unfinished; Israeli intelligence assesses Iran moved thousands of advanced centrifuges into the complex last fall. The threat follows the IAEA's Sept 1-2 warning that it has had no verification access to Iran's enriched uranium stockpile since the war began.

confidenceReason: Direct on-record statement from President Trump; the underlying intelligence claim about centrifuge transfers is attributed to unnamed Israeli intelligence assessments and is not independently verified.
